gaps.what: No dossier written; no borders drawn. The name collects the separate Late Bronze Age kingdoms of Syria (Kadesh, Nuhashshe, Mukish, Niya, Arahtu, Tunip, Qatna, Amurru, Ugarit, Aleppo, Carchemish), each with its own ruler. The new-kingdom-of-egypt events (-1447 vassal_start, -1352 vassal_end) and the hittites -1345 gain should name the individual kingdoms (dossiers exist for qatna, amurru, ugarit, mitanni; missing for kadesh, nuhashshe, mukish) or nobody.

problems: syrian-city-states was not written: it is a collective name for separate kingdoms, not a state (gaps); new-kingdom-of-egypt ledger 6 and 10 and hittites ledger 5 keep a counterpart with no dossier until they are changed to the individual kingdoms or nobody.

principality-of-uglich: the citing events (principality-of-vladimir-suzdal ledger 10, 1389; grand-principality-of-moscow ledger 20 and 35, 1415 and 1482; all confidence 1) rest on Cliopatria shapes; the pages (Uglich, Bezhetsk, Dmitry Donskoy) make the land a Moscow-house appanage from the 1328 sale. Kept as a state 1218-1482 so the dossiers agree; the 1482 end differs from the Ivan III page (arrest 1491, death 1493). A gap-filler should decide whether those three events should name grand-principality-of-moscow or nobody.

kathiri-sultanate vs tahirid-sultanate: Kathiri page has the conquest of Shihr in the 1460s (dossier gain 1465); Tahirid page and Tahirid ledger 5 (confidence 1) have the loss at the end of the 15th century (1499). Not edited in the Tahirid dossier; the later loss finds no land to move.

transcaucasian-democratic-federative-republic: TDFR page dates the Armenian and Azerbaijani declarations 28 May 1918, the Caucasus campaign page 'the same day' as Georgia (26 May). The armenia and azerbaijan-democratic-republic dossiers use 28 May.

principality-of-rostov and principality-of-uglich have no Wikipedia article of their own ('Principality of Rostov' redirects to the Vladimir-Suzdal article; 'Uglich' is the town); wikipedia is null. Their shapes are radius discs round the towns (40 km and 30 km, as the Yaroslavl dossier subtracts) that overlap Cliopatria's Vladimir-Suzdal shapes; the compiler must let the new keyframes win there.

Cliopatria has no row for any of the four; all keyframes are new. No pages failed. One fetch of the 'Rostov' article returned Rostov-on-Don (a wrong title, not used); Rostov Veliky was opened instead.
WebFetch returns a summary of each page, so quotes in notes are the fetch tool's quotations of the page's sentences.
